title: Clionidae platform refresh and shell cleanup
content:
Clionidae had a late-day refresh to bring the template library up to the current JeffersonWM platform instead of leaving it as a June-era snapshot. The work was mostly about truthfulness and usefulness: Clio should now describe the patterns we are actually using, not just the patterns we once planned.

What changed:

  • Current platform language: the visible Clio pages and docs now reflect central Auth / Multimillion, app memberships, popup/full-page auth handoff, richer Feed manual entries, public versions, buildlog/action records, backend sync, and public-only route guards.
  • Template scripts: Clio's package scripts now line up with the newer app-local workflow: version helpers, prompted build logging, version history lookup, and publish commands.
  • Visual direction clarified: Clionidae is now framed as a standards and structure library, not a shared house style. It should help future apps reuse layout, routing, state, and documentation habits while still allowing each site to look radically different.
  • Shell cleanup: the main Clionidae brand links home, the Design page now reads Clionidae Visual + Design Library with only the Clionidae word linking home, footer credits link to JeffersonWM Home and the GitHub account, and the About page/link were removed for now.

What worked was treating Clio as a memory aid for the whole platform. The older template was still useful, but it needed to absorb what Auth, Feed, Aphelion, Perihelion, and the publishing scripts have taught us. What did not need to continue was the half-present About page and the older implication that every JeffersonWM app should share one visual identity.

Verification passed with npm run lint and npm run build. The next Clio question is whether to give this a public version bump before deployment, or keep it as a local standards update until the next visual pass.
